To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the classic formula relating the in situ strength with the fracture toughness is valid only for the case when the ply thickness and the fracture process zone are both small.

the in situ strength can be computed from the fracture toughness and the ply thickness, and that the in situ strengths can be predicted by the R-curve, the ply thickness and the in situ strength in the limit of zero ply thickness.

for a composite with a given fracture process zone, the in situ fracture strength of a ply depends on the ply thickness, and for a given ply thickness, it depends on the fracture toughness of the composite.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and validation of an experimental methodology to determine the fracture toughness of thin composite laminates.
the prediction of in situ strength of a ply in a laminate.
the development of an improved understanding of the mechanics of the fracture process in composite laminates and of the role played by the fracture process zone.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
for the cases of small ply thicknesses, the in situ strengths of the ply can be predicted from the R-curves of the material.
the in situ strengths are predicted by the fracture toughness of the ply, provided the ply thickness is large enough for a fully developed fracture process zone.

the classic approach, which assumes the fracture process zone fully developed within the ply, is valid when the fracture process is not very large, or the thickness of the ply is large enough to allow the complete development of the fracture process zone.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the classic formulation for in situ strengths is not appropriate when the ply size approaches zero.
the in situ strength is not only a function of the fracture toughness but also of the size of the fracture process zone, the latter being related to the ply thickness.
the in situ strength can be computed from the R-curve, but that this is not always possible, and when it is possible, it is not always correct.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the in situ strength is a function of the R-curve and the ply thickness.
, in order to correctly compute the in situ strength, one needs to consider the R-curve and the ply thickness.
the in situ strength is always smaller or equal to the in plane ply strength.
